sandbox.summary: PASS. The patch was applied in an isolated Docker sandbox and pytest exited with code 0. All 7 collected tests passed (7 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors, 0 skipped) in 0.14s on Python 3.11.17 with pytest 9.1.1. The covered tests were: test_index, test_health, test_metrics_endpoint, test_leak_endpoint_responds, test_leak_does_not_retain_memory, test_checkout_healthy_by_default, and test_requests_counted_by_status_and_release. The memory-leak regression test (test_leak_does_not_retain_memory) and the metrics and status/release counting tests passed, so the patched behaviour is consistent with expectations. Caveat: this verdict covers only the 7 tests in test_app.py. Coverage of the patch beyond those tests was not reported, and the run was short (0.14s), so it does not show long-running or load behaviour. The patch is cleared on the basis of the test results provided.

patch.explanation: The root cause is that `leak()` in sample-app/app.py appends a 10 MiB string to the module-level `leak_store` on every request and never releases it. This is why the working set rose from about 24 MB to about 108 MB after 8 calls and triggered the memory_high alert. The patch deletes the intentional-bug comment and the `leak_store.append(...)` line, so /leak still returns HTTP 200 with `{status: ok}` but retains nothing between requests.
